HeroCountdown.remainingSeconds_ceiltheoremagreel.51

remainingSeconds is the ceiling: for a future target it is the least rr with 1000 r≥1000\,r \ge the gap.

∀ now,target∈Z, now<target:1000 (r−1)<target−now≤1000 r,r=remainingSeconds⁡(now,target)\displaystyle \forall\, \mathit{now}, \mathit{target} \in \mathbb{Z},\ \mathit{now} < \mathit{target}:\quad 1000\,(r - 1) < \mathit{target} - \mathit{now} \le 1000\, r,\qquad r = \operatorname{remainingSeconds}(\mathit{now}, \mathit{target})

While the target is ahead, the shown seconds are the gap in ms divided by 1000 and rounded up.

HeroCountdown.remainingSeconds_pasttheoremagreel.65

Zero remaining time: at or after the target the countdown shows 0 seconds.

∀ now,target∈Z:target≤now⇒remainingSeconds⁡(now,target)=0\displaystyle \forall\, \mathit{now}, \mathit{target} \in \mathbb{Z}:\quad \mathit{target} \le \mathit{now} \Rightarrow \operatorname{remainingSeconds}(\mathit{now}, \mathit{target}) = 0

Once the target is reached or passed (including any negative gap), the remaining time is exactly zero.

HeroCountdown.remainingSeconds_antitonetheoremagreel.73

Monotone in time: a later clock never shows more remaining seconds.

∀ t1,t2,target∈Z:t1≤t2⇒remainingSeconds⁡(t2,target)≤remainingSeconds⁡(t1,target)\displaystyle \forall\, t_1, t_2, \mathit{target} \in \mathbb{Z}:\quad t_1 \le t_2 \Rightarrow \operatorname{remainingSeconds}(t_2, \mathit{target}) \le \operatorname{remainingSeconds}(t_1, \mathit{target})

As time moves forward the remaining seconds never go up.

HeroCountdown.unitsFromSeconds_rangetheoremagreel.99

Range bounds: hours below 24, minutes and seconds below 60.

∀n∈N, [d,h,m,s]=unitsFromSeconds⁡(n):h<24∧m<60∧s<60\displaystyle \forall n \in \mathbb{N},\ [d, h, m, s] = \operatorname{unitsFromSeconds}(n):\quad h < 24 \land m < 60 \land s < 60

The hour, minute and second fields always stay inside a clock's normal range.

HeroCountdown.unitsFromSeconds_sumtheoremagreel.108

The units add back up to the total.

∀n∈N, [d,h,m,s]=unitsFromSeconds⁡(n):86400 d+3600 h+60 m+s=n\displaystyle \forall n \in \mathbb{N},\ [d, h, m, s] = \operatorname{unitsFromSeconds}(n):\quad 86400\,d + 3600\,h + 60\,m + s = n

Nothing is lost or double counted when seconds are split into days, hours, minutes and seconds.

HeroCountdown.unitsFromSeconds_monotheoremagreel.128

Monotone display: fewer remaining seconds give a lexicographically smaller (or equal) reading.

∀a,b∈N:a≤b⇒unitsFromSeconds⁡(a)⪯unitsFromSeconds⁡(b)\displaystyle \forall a, b \in \mathbb{N}:\quad a \le b \Rightarrow \operatorname{unitsFromSeconds}(a) \preceq \operatorname{unitsFromSeconds}(b)

The shown days/hours/minutes/seconds tick down in clock order whenever the remaining seconds go down.

HeroCountdown.countdown_mono_in_timetheoremagreel.137

Monotonicity in time, end to end: a later clock shows a reading no later in clock order.

∀t1≤t2, target∈Z:units⁡(remainingSeconds⁡(t2,target))⪯units⁡(remainingSeconds⁡(t1,target))\displaystyle \forall t_1 \le t_2,\ \mathit{target} \in \mathbb{Z}:\quad \operatorname{units}(\operatorname{remainingSeconds}(t_2, \mathit{target})) \preceq \operatorname{units}(\operatorname{remainingSeconds}(t_1, \mathit{target}))

As the clock advances, the countdown display never moves backwards.

HeroCountdown.lt_pow_digitCounttheoremagreel.161

Every number is below 10 to the power of its digit count.

∀m∈N:m<10digitCount⁡(m)\displaystyle \forall m \in \mathbb{N}:\quad m < 10^{\operatorname{digitCount}(m)}

A number always fits in as many decimal places as it has digits.

HeroCountdown.digitAt_lt_tentheoremagreel.220

Every shown digit is a decimal digit.

∀v∈Q,p∈N:digitAt⁡(v,p)<10\displaystyle \forall v \in \mathbb{Q}, p \in \mathbb{N}:\quad \operatorname{digitAt}(v, p) < 10

A digit cell never needs a face outside 0-9.

HeroCountdown.foldl_placestheoremagreel.234

Reading the digits at the first n places from an accumulator.

∀m,n,a: foldl⁡(λx d. 10x+d, a, [⌊m/p⌋ mod 10∣p∈places⁡(n)])=a⋅10n+(m mod 10n)\displaystyle \forall m, n, a:\ \operatorname{foldl}(\lambda x\,d.\ 10x + d,\ a,\ [\lfloor m/p \rfloor \bmod 10 \mid p \in \operatorname{places}(n)]) = a \cdot 10^n + (m \bmod 10^n)
HeroCountdown.digits_spell_valuetheoremagreel.245

The shown digits spell the value: reading the digit row gives back ∣⌊v⌋∣|\lfloor v \rfloor|, padded or not.

∀v∈Q,p∈{⊤,⊥}:fromDigits⁡([digitAt⁡(v,q)∣q∈digitPlaces⁡(v,p)])=∣⌊v⌋∣\displaystyle \forall v \in \mathbb{Q}, p \in \{\top, \bot\}:\quad \operatorname{fromDigits}\big([\operatorname{digitAt}(v, q) \mid q \in \operatorname{digitPlaces}(v, p)]\big) = |\lfloor v \rfloor|

The digits a unit displays always read back as exactly the unit's value (padding only adds leading zeros).

HeroCountdown.fmod10_boundstheoremagreel.271

The floored remainder lies on the dial.

∀x∈Q: 0≤fmod⁡10(x)<10\displaystyle \forall x \in \mathbb{Q}:\ 0 \le \operatorname{fmod}_{10}(x) < 10
HeroCountdown.fmod10_eqtheoremagreel.279

The floored remainder differs from its argument by whole turns.

∀x ∃z∈Z: fmod⁡10(x)=x−10z\displaystyle \forall x\ \exists z \in \mathbb{Z}:\ \operatorname{fmod}_{10}(x) = x - 10 z
HeroCountdown.faceDelta_boundstheoremagreel.300

Faces lie in the half-open band (−5,5](-5, 5] cells.

∀k∈Z,a∈Q:−5<faceDelta⁡(k,a)≤5\displaystyle \forall k \in \mathbb{Z}, a \in \mathbb{Q}:\quad -5 < \operatorname{faceDelta}(k, a) \le 5

Every face is at most five cells from the window, so each face has one position per spring value.

HeroCountdown.faceDelta_congrtheoremagreel.311

Faces are congruent to k−ak - a modulo 10.

∀k∈Z,a∈Q ∃z∈Z:faceDelta⁡(k,a)=k−a+10z\displaystyle \forall k \in \mathbb{Z}, a \in \mathbb{Q}\ \exists z \in \mathbb{Z}:\quad \operatorname{faceDelta}(k, a) = k - a + 10 z

A face's offset always equals its digit minus the spring value, up to whole turns of the 10-digit dial.

HeroCountdown.int_eq_zero_of_lt_onetheoremagreel.329

An integer strictly between -1 and 1 is 0.

∀z∈Z: −1<z<1⇒z=0\displaystyle \forall z \in \mathbb{Z}:\ -1 < z < 1 \Rightarrow z = 0
HeroCountdown.eq_of_congr10theoremagreel.337

Two values congruent mod 10 inside the same width-10 band are equal.

x=y+10z, x,y∈(−5,5], z∈Z⇒x=y\displaystyle x = y + 10z,\ x, y \in (-5, 5],\ z \in \mathbb{Z} \Rightarrow x = y
HeroCountdown.strip_shows_sametheoremagreel.368

**Strip shows the same as faithful.** Inside the digit window (offsets strictly between −1-1 and 11 cell, the only ones the clip lets through) the strip shows digit k at offset o exactly when the faithful face k sits at o, for every spring value.

∀a∈Q, k∈{0..9}, o∈(−1,1):(∃j∈{0..11}: stripEntryDigit⁡(j)=k∧j+stripOffsetCells⁡(a)=o)  ⟺  faceDelta⁡(k,a)=o\displaystyle \forall a \in \mathbb{Q},\ k \in \{0..9\},\ o \in (-1, 1):\quad \big(\exists j \in \{0..11\}:\ \operatorname{stripEntryDigit}(j) = k \land j + \operatorname{stripOffsetCells}(a) = o\big) \iff \operatorname{faceDelta}(k, a) = o

Whatever the spring is doing, the visible part of the strip is the same picture as the visible faces of the original: same digits at the same positions (multiply by c>0c > 0 for pixels).

HeroCountdown.faceDelta_settledtheoremagreel.412

Settled digits: with the spring at rest on digit d, face d sits at offset 0 and no other face does.

∀d,k∈{0..9}:faceDelta⁡(k,d)=0  ⟺  k=d\displaystyle \forall d, k \in \{0..9\}:\quad \operatorname{faceDelta}(k, d) = 0 \iff k = d

When the spring has settled, the digit it was told to show is the one face at offset 0.

HeroCountdown.springStep_donetheoremagreel.504

A settled spring is exactly on target with zero velocity.

∀s,x∗,dt:springStep⁡(s,x∗,dt).done⇒springStep⁡(s,x∗,dt).s=(x∗,0)\displaystyle \forall s, x^\ast, \mathit{dt}:\quad \operatorname{springStep}(s, x^\ast, \mathit{dt}).\mathit{done} \Rightarrow \operatorname{springStep}(s, x^\ast, \mathit{dt}).s = (x^\ast, 0)

When the roll ends, the digit sits exactly on its cell, which is why the settled faces land on whole pixels.

HeroCountdown.slices_nonpostheoremagreel.515

A non-positive frame gap runs no slice.

∀dt∈Q, dt≤0:slices⁡(dt)=0\displaystyle \forall \mathit{dt} \in \mathbb{Q},\ \mathit{dt} \le 0:\quad \operatorname{slices}(\mathit{dt}) = 0

If no time passed, the slice loop runs zero times.

HeroCountdown.countdownMetrics_celltheoremagreel.579

The cell heights in the metrics table are cellHeight of the band's font.

∀ℓ,c:metrics⁡(ℓ,c).c=cellHeight⁡(metrics⁡(ℓ,c).font)\displaystyle \forall \ell, c:\quad \operatorname{metrics}(\ell, c).c = \operatorname{cellHeight}(\operatorname{metrics}(\ell, c).\mathit{font})

[d,h,m,s]⪯[d′,h′,m′,s′]  ⟺  d<d′∨(d=d′∧(h<h′∨(h=h′∧(m<m′∨(m=m′∧s≤s′))))),x⪯y is false if ∣x∣≠4∨∣y∣≠4\displaystyle [d,h,m,s] \preceq [d',h',m',s'] \iff d < d' \lor (d = d' \land (h < h' \lor (h = h' \land (m < m' \lor (m = m' \land s \le s'))))),\qquad x \preceq y \text{ is false if } |x| \ne 4 \lor |y| \ne 4

HeroCountdown.Springinductiveagreel.435

HeroExit

hero.exit: scroll position → exit opacity, scatter and the CSS consumers (M2 pilot part)Fw/Parts/HeroExit.lean · 20 theorems · 21 definitions · 41/41 reviewed
HeroExit.div_mul_postheoremagreel.27

Division by a positive number undoes multiplication.

∀c,n∈Q, n>0:cn⋅n=c\displaystyle \forall c, n \in \mathbb{Q},\ n > 0:\quad \tfrac{c}{n}\cdot n = c

Dividing and multiplying back by the same positive number gives the original value.

HeroExit.div_unittheoremagreel.34

A share between 0 and the whole is a fraction between 0 and 1.

∀c,n∈Q, n>0, 0≤c≤n:0≤cn≤1\displaystyle \forall c, n \in \mathbb{Q},\ n > 0,\ 0 \le c \le n:\quad 0 \le \tfrac{c}{n} \le 1

Part of a positive length divided by the length lies in the unit interval.

HeroExit.div_monotheoremagreel.49

Dividing by a positive number keeps order.

∀c1,c2,n∈Q, n>0:c1≤c2⇒c1n≤c2n\displaystyle \forall c_1, c_2, n \in \mathbb{Q},\ n > 0:\quad c_1 \le c_2 \Rightarrow \tfrac{c_1}{n} \le \tfrac{c_2}{n}

A larger numerator over the same positive denominator is never a smaller fraction.

HeroExit.exitRange_postheoremagreel.94

The exit range is positive.

∀h,v: 0<max⁡(1,h−v)\displaystyle \forall h, v:\ 0 < \max(1, h - v)
HeroExit.exitOpacity_memtheoremagreel.97

Clamping: the exit opacity is always in [0,1][0, 1].

∀t,h,v∈Q:0≤exitOpacity⁡(t,h,v)≤1\displaystyle \forall t, h, v \in \mathbb{Q}:\quad 0 \le \operatorname{exitOpacity}(t, h, v) \le 1

Whatever the track geometry and scroll position, the opacity written is a valid opacity.

HeroExit.exitOpacity_antitonetheoremagreel.115

Monotone in scroll: scrolling further down never raises the opacity.

∀T,h,v,y1,y2∈Q:y1≤y2⇒exitOpacityAt⁡(T,h,v,y2)≤exitOpacityAt⁡(T,h,v,y1)\displaystyle \forall T, h, v, y_1, y_2 \in \mathbb{Q}:\quad y_1 \le y_2 \Rightarrow \operatorname{exitOpacityAt}(T, h, v, y_2) \le \operatorname{exitOpacityAt}(T, h, v, y_1)

The hero only fades out as you scroll down, and only fades back in as you scroll up.

HeroExit.exitOpacity_lipschitztheoremagreel.127

Lipschitz in scroll (hence continuous, including at both clamp edges y=Ty = T and y=T+ny = T + n): the opacity changes by at most ∣Δy∣/n|\Delta y| / n.

∀T,h,v, y1≤y2:0≤n (exitOpacityAt⁡(y1)−exitOpacityAt⁡(y2))≤y2−y1,n=max⁡(1,h−v)\displaystyle \forall T, h, v,\ y_1 \le y_2:\quad 0 \le n\,\big(\operatorname{exitOpacityAt}(y_1) - \operatorname{exitOpacityAt}(y_2)\big) \le y_2 - y_1,\quad n = \max(1, h - v)

The fade has no jumps: one px of scroll moves the opacity by at most one n-th.

HeroExit.exitOpacity_beforetheoremagreel.146

Before the exit: with the track top at or below the viewport top, the hero is fully opaque.

∀t≥0, h,v:exitOpacity⁡(t,h,v)=1\displaystyle \forall t \ge 0,\ h, v:\quad \operatorname{exitOpacity}(t, h, v) = 1

Nothing fades until the track starts to scroll past the top of the viewport.

HeroExit.exitOpacity_aftertheoremagreel.157

After the exit: once scrolled through the whole range, the hero is fully transparent.

∀t,h,v:−t≥max⁡(1,h−v)⇒exitOpacity⁡(t,h,v)=0\displaystyle \forall t, h, v:\quad -t \ge \max(1, h - v) \Rightarrow \operatorname{exitOpacity}(t, h, v) = 0

Past the end of the range the opacity stays at exactly 0.

HeroExit.exitOpacity_lineartheoremagreel.168

Inside the range the fade is linear: n e=n+tn\,e = n + t.

∀t,h,v:0≤−t≤n⇒n⋅exitOpacity⁡(t,h,v)=n+t,n=max⁡(1,h−v)\displaystyle \forall t, h, v:\quad 0 \le -t \le n \Rightarrow n \cdot \operatorname{exitOpacity}(t, h, v) = n + t,\quad n = \max(1, h - v)

Between the two clamp edges the opacity falls in a straight line with the scroll offset.

HeroExit.pointerOff_monotheoremagreel.222

Pointer-off is an upper set in scroll: once off, scrolling further keeps it off.

∀T,h,v, y1≤y2:pointerOff⁡(exitOpacityAt⁡(y1))⇒pointerOff⁡(exitOpacityAt⁡(y2))\displaystyle \forall T, h, v,\ y_1 \le y_2:\quad \operatorname{pointerOff}(\operatorname{exitOpacityAt}(y_1)) \Rightarrow \operatorname{pointerOff}(\operatorname{exitOpacityAt}(y_2))

Once the hero ignores taps, scrolling further down keeps it that way; it never flickers back on while scrolling down.

HeroExit.pointerOff_iff_thresholdtheoremagreel.235

The pointer-off threshold: pointer events are off exactly when the scroll is strictly past T+1920nT + \tfrac{19}{20} n.

∀T,h,v,y∈Q:pointerOff⁡(exitOpacityAt⁡(T,h,v,y))  ⟺  y>T+1920 n,n=max⁡(1,h−v)\displaystyle \forall T, h, v, y \in \mathbb{Q}:\quad \operatorname{pointerOff}(\operatorname{exitOpacityAt}(T, h, v, y)) \iff y > T + \tfrac{19}{20}\,n,\quad n = \max(1, h - v)

There is a single scroll position, 95% of the way through the exit range, past which the hero ignores taps.

HeroExit.navHeroProgress_eqtheoremagreel.272

The two code sites agree: the nav's progress is exactly one minus the exit opacity.

∀t,h,v:navHeroProgress⁡(t,h,v)=1−exitOpacity⁡(t,h,v)\displaystyle \forall t, h, v:\quad \operatorname{navHeroProgress}(t, h, v) = 1 - \operatorname{exitOpacity}(t, h, v)

The original computes the hero progress twice; both are the same number, so one owner can serve both.

HeroExit.pill_thresholdtheoremagreel.280

The 0.72 flip (is-hero-pill off, people reveal, pain dark) in exit-opacity terms.

∀t,h,v:navHeroProgress⁡(t,h,v)≥1825  ⟺  exitOpacity⁡(t,h,v)≤725\displaystyle \forall t, h, v:\quad \operatorname{navHeroProgress}(t, h, v) \ge \tfrac{18}{25} \iff \operatorname{exitOpacity}(t, h, v) \le \tfrac{7}{25}

The nav's 0.72 threshold is the moment the hero's opacity drops to 0.28.

HeroExit.pointerOff_after_pilltheoremagreel.288

The hero's pointer cut-off comes after the 0.72 flip.

∀t,h,v:pointerOff⁡(exitOpacity⁡(t,h,v))⇒navHeroProgress⁡(t,h,v)≥1825\displaystyle \forall t, h, v:\quad \operatorname{pointerOff}(\operatorname{exitOpacity}(t, h, v)) \Rightarrow \operatorname{navHeroProgress}(t, h, v) \ge \tfrac{18}{25}

By the time the hero ignores taps, the nav has already dropped its hero pill.

HeroExit.exitRange_200vhtheoremagreel.323

With a 200vh track and innerHeight = vh, the exit range is the viewport height (at least 1).

∀v:exitRange⁡(2v,v)=max⁡(1,v)\displaystyle \forall v:\quad \operatorname{exitRange}(2v, v) = \max(1, v)

On desktop the hero fades over exactly one screen of scrolling.

HeroExit.cue_ts_eq_fulltheoremagreel.386

The TS reading of the cue is the full reading in the settled state (cue entered; above 600 px, splash done).

∀c,s,ℓ,d: (ℓ⇒c=1)∧(¬ℓ⇒d)⇒cueBlurPx⁡(s)=cueBlurPxFull⁡(c,s,ℓ,d)∧cueTranslateYPx⁡(s,ℓ)=cueTranslateYPxFull⁡(c,s,ℓ,d)\displaystyle \forall c, s, \ell, d:\ (\ell \Rightarrow c = 1) \land (\lnot\ell \Rightarrow d) \Rightarrow \operatorname{cueBlurPx}(s) = \operatorname{cueBlurPxFull}(c, s, \ell, d) \land \operatorname{cueTranslateYPx}(s, \ell) = \operatorname{cueTranslateYPxFull}(c, s, \ell, d)

The two readings differ only during the load entrance, never while the user scrolls a settled page.

HeroExit.consumers_rangetheoremagreel.412

Ranges of the settled consumers for e∈[0,1]e \in [0,1] (s=1−es = 1 - e, copyIn∈[0,1]\mathit{copyIn} \in [0,1]).

∀c,e∈[0,1]:0≤c e≤1∧1320≤cardOpacity⁡(1−e)≤1\displaystyle \forall c, e \in [0,1]:\quad 0 \le c\,e \le 1 \land \tfrac{13}{20} \le \operatorname{cardOpacity}(1 - e) \le 1

Copy and card opacities stay valid opacities, and cards never dim below 65%.

HeroExit.consumers_monotheoremagreel.425

Monotone in scroll, per band: as ss grows, translations move up (decrease), blurs grow, opacities fall.

∀c,ℓ, 0≤c, s1≤s2:copyTranslateYPx⁡(c,s2,ℓ)≤copyTranslateYPx⁡(c,s1,ℓ)∧copyBlurPx⁡(c,s1,ℓ)≤copyBlurPx⁡(c,s2,ℓ)∧cardOpacity⁡(s2)≤cardOpacity⁡(s1)∧copyOpacity⁡(c,1−s2)≤copyOpacity⁡(c,1−s1)\displaystyle \forall c, \ell,\ 0 \le c,\ s_1 \le s_2:\quad \operatorname{copyTranslateYPx}(c, s_2, \ell) \le \operatorname{copyTranslateYPx}(c, s_1, \ell) \land \operatorname{copyBlurPx}(c, s_1, \ell) \le \operatorname{copyBlurPx}(c, s_2, \ell) \land \operatorname{cardOpacity}(s_2) \le \operatorname{cardOpacity}(s_1) \land \operatorname{copyOpacity}(c, 1 - s_2) \le \operatorname{copyOpacity}(c, 1 - s_1)

Every exit effect moves in one direction as the page scrolls down, in both bands.

HeroExit.band_edge_jumptheoremagreel.441

The band edge at 600 px is a jump unless the hero is at rest: settled copy (c=1c = 1) moves −8s-8s vs −10s-10s and blurs 00 vs 18s18 s; the settled cue moves −10s-10 s vs 00.

∀s:copyTranslateYPx⁡(1,s,⊤)−copyTranslateYPx⁡(1,s,⊥)=2s∧copyBlurPx⁡(1,s,⊥)−copyBlurPx⁡(1,s,⊤)=18s∧cueTranslateYPx⁡(s,⊥)−cueTranslateYPx⁡(s,⊤)=10s\displaystyle \forall s:\quad \operatorname{copyTranslateYPx}(1, s, \top) - \operatorname{copyTranslateYPx}(1, s, \bot) = 2 s \land \operatorname{copyBlurPx}(1, s, \bot) - \operatorname{copyBlurPx}(1, s, \top) = 18 s \land \operatorname{cueTranslateYPx}(s, \bot) - \operatorname{cueTranslateYPx}(s, \top) = 10 s

Resizing across 600 px mid-exit makes the copy and cue jump; at the top of the page (s=0s = 0) the two bands agree.

BreakpointFacts

Facts about the 30 breakpoint conditionsFw/Site/BreakpointFacts.lean · 55 theorems · 3 definitions · 57/58 reviewed
Breakpoints.catalogue_lengththeoremagreel.20

The catalogue has the inventory's 30 media conditions.

∣catalogue∣=30\displaystyle |\mathrm{catalogue}| = 30

There are exactly thirty conditions.

Breakpoints.catalogue_ids_noduptheoremagreel.27

Inventory ids and TS ids are pairwise distinct.

i≠j⇒idi≠idj∧tsi≠tsj\displaystyle i \ne j \Rightarrow \mathrm{id}_i \ne \mathrm{id}_j \land \mathrm{ts}_i \ne \mathrm{ts}_j

No two conditions share a name.

Breakpoints.catalogue_queries_noduptheoremagreel.34

No two catalogue entries are the same query.

i≠j⇒qi≠qj\displaystyle i \ne j \Rightarrow q_i \ne q_j

The thirty conditions are syntactically distinct.

Breakpoints.catalogue_csstheoremagreel.41

**Byte-exact CSS.** The printed normal form of every condition equals the inventory's condition string (breakpoints.json, schema fw.breakpoints/1, ids mq.*).

∀i<30. (idi,tsi,css(qi))=(idiinv,ti,siinv),t=(rmReduce,rmNopref,…,c1000Nodw)\displaystyle \forall i < 30.\ (\mathrm{id}_i, \mathrm{ts}_i, \mathrm{css}(q_i)) = (\mathrm{id}^{inv}_i, t_i, s^{inv}_i),\quad t = (\texttt{rmReduce}, \texttt{rmNopref}, \dots, \texttt{c1000Nodw})

where tt is the list of TS ids written in the theorem (breakpoints.json has no TS-id field).

Each condition prints exactly as the inventory writes it, under the listed TS id.

Breakpoints.catalogue_edgestheoremagreel.82

**Edges.** The tagged edges read off each condition's syntax equal the inventory's edges list (feature, lower pixel of the pair N | N+1).

∀i<30. E(qi)=Eiinv\displaystyle \forall i < 30.\ E(q_i) = E^{inv}_i

Every condition has exactly the edges the inventory lists, in the same order.

Breakpoints.catalogue_axis_edgestheoremagreel.121

The width edges and device-width edges used by MQ.eval_congr are exactly the tagged edge pixels (per axis), and the tagged edges are the inventory's by catalogue_edges.

∀i<30. {N∣N∈Ew(qi)}={N∣(a,N)∈E(qi), a∈{width,width(touch)}}∧{N∣N∈Ed(qi)}={N∣(device-width,N)∈E(qi)}\displaystyle \forall i < 30.\ \{N \mid N \in E_w(q_i)\} = \{N \mid (a, N) \in E(q_i),\ a \in \{\text{width}, \text{width(touch)}\}\} \land \{N \mid N \in E_d(q_i)\} = \{N \mid (\text{device-width}, N) \in E(q_i)\}

(and E(qi)=EiinvE(q_i) = E^{inv}_i by catalogue_edges).

The edges in the sufficiency theorem are the tagged edges, hence the inventory's edges, no more and no fewer.

Breakpoints.MQ.eval_indep_height_dprtheoremagreel.385

Height, device height and DPR never change any condition.

∀q,e,h′,dh′,r′:⟦q⟧e[h:=h′, dh:=dh′, r:=r′]=⟦q⟧e\displaystyle \forall q, e, h', d_h', r':\quad \llbracket q \rrbracket_{e[h:=h',\,d_h:=d_h',\,r:=r']} = \llbracket q \rrbracket_e

The page has no height, device-height or resolution media query, so these inputs never change a media condition (height can still change layout through vh units and JS viewport-height reads).

Breakpoints.c860_le_c1000_le_c1030theoremagreel.404

The combos are nested: combo 860 implies combo 1000, which implies combo 1030.

e⊨C860⇒e⊨C1000∧e⊨C1000⇒e⊨C1030\displaystyle e \models C_{860} \Rightarrow e \models C_{1000} \quad\land\quad e \models C_{1000} \Rightarrow e \models C_{1030}

A wider combo matches wherever a narrower one does.

Breakpoints.c1000Nodw_vs_c1000theoremagreel.423

c1000Nodw implies c1000, and they differ exactly for a small screen, a viewport above 1000 px, and no matching touch arm.

(e⊨C1000nodw⇒e⊨C1000)∧(e⊨C1000∧e⊭C1000nodw  ⟺  dw≤500∧w>1000∧¬(touch(e)∧w≤1200))\displaystyle (e \models C^{nodw}_{1000} \Rightarrow e \models C_{1000}) \land (e \models C_{1000} \land e \not\models C^{nodw}_{1000} \iff d_w \le 500 \land w > 1000 \land \neg(\mathrm{touch}(e) \land w \le 1200))

The countdown's combo is the commission combo minus the device-width arm, and only that arm separates them.

Breakpoints.overlap_c860_wGe861theoremagreel.457

**Overlap C860 / >=861.** Both match exactly on a viewport of at least 861 px with a small screen or a touch input up to 1200 px.

e⊨C860∧e⊨(w≥861)  ⟺  w≥861∧(dw≤500∨(touch(e)∧w≤1200))\displaystyle e \models C_{860} \land e \models (w \ge 861) \iff w \ge 861 \land (d_w \le 500 \lor (\mathrm{touch}(e) \land w \le 1200))

A touch tablet at 861-1200 px or a phone in landscape takes both the compact and the desktop rules.

Breakpoints.overlap_c1000_wGe1001theoremagreel.477

**Overlap C1000 / >=1001.** Both match exactly on a viewport of at least 1001 px with a small screen or a touch input up to 1200 px.

e⊨C1000∧e⊨(w≥1001)  ⟺  w≥1001∧(dw≤500∨(touch(e)∧w≤1200))\displaystyle e \models C_{1000} \land e \models (w \ge 1001) \iff w \ge 1001 \land (d_w \le 500 \lor (\mathrm{touch}(e) \land w \le 1200))

Commission compact and the desktop platform mission title apply together on a touch tablet at 1001-1200 px.

Breakpoints.overlap_c1000_wGe1001Nopreftheoremagreel.497

**Overlap C1000 / >=1001 and no-preference.** As overlap_c1000_wGe1001, plus motion allowed.

e⊨C1000∧e⊨(w≥1001∧μ=no-preference)  ⟺  w≥1001∧μ=no-preference∧(dw≤500∨(touch(e)∧w≤1200))\displaystyle e \models C_{1000} \land e \models (w \ge 1001 \land \mu = \text{no-preference}) \iff w \ge 1001 \land \mu = \text{no-preference} \land (d_w \le 500 \lor (\mathrm{touch}(e) \land w \le 1200))

The sticky desktop commission and the compact commission both match on a touch tablet at 1001-1200 px with motion on.

Breakpoints.c860_not_wLe860theoremagreel.517

**Never mix pure 860 and C860.** C860 holds while (width<=860px) fails exactly above 860 px with a small screen or a touch input up to 1200 px.

e⊨C860∧e⊭(w≤860)  ⟺  w>860∧(dw≤500∨(touch(e)∧w≤1200))\displaystyle e \models C_{860} \land e \not\models (w \le 860) \iff w > 860 \land (d_w \le 500 \lor (\mathrm{touch}(e) \land w \le 1200))

Pure-width users take the desktop path where combo users take the compact path, so one cannot stand in for the other.

Breakpoints.wLe860_imp_c860theoremagreel.537

(width<=860px) implies C860 (the converse fails, see c860_not_wLe860).

e⊨(w≤860)⇒e⊨C860\displaystyle e \models (w \le 860) \Rightarrow e \models C_{860}

Every phone-width viewport is also in the combo.

Breakpoints.deskDeck_ifftheoremagreel.554

The desktop deck runs exactly on a viewport of at least 861 px, a screen wider than 500 px, no touch arm, and motion allowed.

deskDeck(e)  ⟺  w≥861∧dw>500∧¬(touch(e)∧w≤1200)∧μ≠reduce\displaystyle \mathrm{deskDeck}(e) \iff w \ge 861 \land d_w > 500 \land \neg(\mathrm{touch}(e) \land w \le 1200) \land \mu \ne \text{reduce}

The JS resolves the CSS overlap in favour of the compact deck on touch tablets and small screens.

Breakpoints.touchTablet_overlaptheoremagreel.578

On a touch tablet at 861-1200 px the CSS overlap holds and the JS desktop deck is off.

touch(e)∧861≤w≤1200⇒e⊨C860∧e⊨(w≥861)∧¬deskDeck(e)\displaystyle \mathrm{touch}(e) \land 861 \le w \le 1200 \Rightarrow e \models C_{860} \land e \models (w \ge 861) \land \neg\mathrm{deskDeck}(e)

Touch tablets get the compact JS deck while both CSS paths match.

Breakpoints.smallScreen_overlaptheoremagreel.588

On a small screen (phone landscape) above 860 px the CSS overlap holds and the JS desktop deck is off.

dw≤500∧w≥861⇒e⊨C860∧e⊨(w≥861)∧¬deskDeck(e)\displaystyle d_w \le 500 \land w \ge 861 \Rightarrow e \models C_{860} \land e \models (w \ge 861) \land \neg\mathrm{deskDeck}(e)

A phone in landscape takes both CSS paths and the compact JS deck.

Breakpoints.gap_ifftheoremagreel.610

**The gaps are real.** For every edge N, a width strictly between N and N+1 matches neither (width<=Npx) nor (width>=N+1px), and those are exactly the widths that match neither.

¬(w≤N)∧¬(w≥N+1)  ⟺  N<w<N+1,N<N+12<N+1\displaystyle \neg(w \le N) \land \neg(w \ge N{+}1) \iff N < w < N{+}1, \qquad N < N{+}\tfrac12 < N{+}1

Between the last pixel of a band and the first pixel of the next lies an open interval that neither side claims.

Breakpoints.no_gap_ofNattheoremagreel.622

At whole-pixel widths there is no gap: (width<=Npx) and (width>=N+1px) are complementary.

∀k∈N. k≤N  ⟺  ¬(k≥N+1)\displaystyle \forall k \in \mathbb{N}.\ k \le N \iff \neg(k \ge N{+}1)

Integer probes can never land in a fractional gap.

Breakpoints.half_boundstheoremagreel.630

A length of value N+12N + \tfrac12 lies strictly between NN and N+1N+1, in any representation.

∀N,p,q∈N, q>0:2p=(2N+1) q⇒Nq<p∧p<(N+1) q\displaystyle \forall N, p, q \in \mathbb{N},\ q > 0:\quad 2p = (2N+1)\,q \Rightarrow N q < p \land p < (N+1)\,q

Breakpoints

Breakpoints of the original homepage, as decidable predicatesFw/Site/Breakpoints.lean · 5 theorems · 80 definitions · 85/85 reviewed
Breakpoints.Feature.holds_congrtheoremagreel.612

A single feature keeps its value when no cut of it separates the two environments.

e∼e′∧(∀N∈Ew(f). SameSideN(w,w′))∧(∀N∈Ed(f). SameSideN(dw,dw′))⇒⟦f⟧e=⟦f⟧e′\displaystyle e \sim e' \land (\forall N \in E_w(f).\ \mathrm{SameSide}_N(w,w')) \land (\forall N \in E_d(f).\ \mathrm{SameSide}_N(d_w,d_w')) \Rightarrow \llbracket f\rrbracket_e = \llbracket f\rrbracket_{e'}

A feature can only flip across one of its own edges.

Breakpoints.MQ.eval_congrtheoremagreel.653

**Edge sufficiency (rational widths).** A query keeps its value between two environments that agree on the discrete features and are on the same side of every width edge and every device-width edge of the query.

e∼e′∧(∀N∈Ew(q). SameSideN(w,w′))∧(∀N∈Ed(q). SameSideN(dw,dw′))⇒⟦q⟧e=⟦q⟧e′\displaystyle e \sim e' \land (\forall N \in E_w(q).\ \mathrm{SameSide}_N(w,w')) \land (\forall N \in E_d(q).\ \mathrm{SameSide}_N(d_w,d_w')) \Rightarrow \llbracket q\rrbracket_e = \llbracket q\rrbracket_{e'}

The truth value of any condition changes only at the edges listed by its syntax.

Breakpoints.sameSide_ofNattheoremagreel.672

For whole-pixel widths, being on the same side of edge N is just comparing with N.

SameSideN(a/1,b/1)  ⟺  (a≤N⇔b≤N)(a,b∈N)\displaystyle \mathrm{SameSide}_N(a/1, b/1) \iff (a \le N \Leftrightarrow b \le N) \qquad (a, b \in \mathbb{N})

At integer widths the two cuts of an edge coincide, so the pair N | N+1 is the whole edge.

Breakpoints.MQ.eval_ofNat_congrtheoremagreel.681

**Edge sufficiency (whole pixels).** At integer widths and device widths, a query has the same value at any two sizes that compare the same way with every edge of the query; so between consecutive edges it is constant and probing N and N+1 at each edge N observes every change.

e∼e′∧(∀N∈Ew(q). a≤N⇔b≤N)∧(∀N∈Ed(q). c≤N⇔d≤N)⇒⟦q⟧e[w:=a, dw:=c]=⟦q⟧e′[w:=b, dw:=d](a,b,c,d∈N)\displaystyle e \sim e' \land (\forall N \in E_w(q).\ a \le N \Leftrightarrow b \le N) \land (\forall N \in E_d(q).\ c \le N \Leftrightarrow d \le N) \Rightarrow \llbracket q\rrbracket_{e[w:=a,\,d_w:=c]} = \llbracket q\rrbracket_{e'[w:=b,\,d_w:=d]} \qquad (a,b,c,d \in \mathbb{N})

Whole-pixel widths in the same band between edges give the same answer.

Breakpoints.MQ.eval_const_on_bandtheoremagreel.696

**Bands.** If no width edge N of q satisfies a ≤ N < b, then q has the same value at every whole-pixel width from a to b (device width and discrete features fixed).

(∀N∈Ew(q). ¬(a≤N<b))∧a≤x≤b⇒⟦q⟧e[w:=a]=⟦q⟧e[w:=x](a,b,x∈N)\displaystyle (\forall N \in E_w(q).\ \neg(a \le N < b)) \land a \le x \le b \Rightarrow \llbracket q\rrbracket_{e[w:=a]} = \llbracket q\rrbracket_{e[w:=x]} \qquad (a,b,x \in \mathbb{N})

Between two consecutive edges a condition is constant.

A small roster, each role on the right model

Roles are committed agent files in .claude/agents/, each with its model, effort, context cap and write paths; pnpm fw roster:check keeps this table equal to the files. Scripts and hooks take over v1's routing, polling and device chores.

RoleModel · effortRuns asWrites
leadopus · mediummain sessionlands on main with fw land; decision records; commits
engine-researcheropus · highteammateresearch notes, refs, fixtures
source-locatorsonnet · lowsubagentnothing
ref-librarian, Explorehaiku · lowsubagentrefs (librarian); nothing (Explore)
part-buildersonnet · mediumnamed worktree subagentone part; Opus per call for engine, morph, the MUI theme and AOT census
console-buildersonnet · mediumnamed worktree subagentconsole apps, paired with the lean-prover that owns the behaviour
measure-engineersonnet · highnamed worktree subagentmeasurement and model packages; Opus per call for the fit and N0–N5
lean-proveropus · highnamed worktree subagent, up to 3 in M0–M2lean/** except the math lock
experiment-ownersonnet · mediumteammate, ≤ 5 in M5experiment cards, presets
revieweropus · mediumfresh subagent, read-onlynothing; its verdict is its reply
math-revieweropus · highfresh subagent, read-onlynothing; its only output is fw math:sign or a disagreement report
researcheropus · highteammateresearch notes
env-opssonnet · mediumteammatethis Mac's toolchain, Homebrew first

page-writeropus · mediumteammateexplainer pages, never the generated math view
no agent—scripts + hooksgates, usage meter, device runs, watchers, queue order, land queue

At most 5 teammates and 8 worktree subagents alive at once (up to 3 of them lean-provers in M0–M2), with 10 subagents as a backstop. The real limit is this Mac's 16 GB of RAM. Fable is used per call only, behind an ask rule.

The only inputs agents have: typed, refusable commands

WhoCommands (each one event; the Lean reducer accepts or refuses it)
the userstep answer or cancel; proposal decision; priority list; session booking; decision answer; best-build pick; thread posts and "answered"; math:sign
leadcard approve; fw land (refused unless the card is land-ready); card drop with a reason; rulings; queue move with a reason
ownercard open; park until a typed condition; wait on an agent; ask the lead; hand-back result (landed, no-gain, refuted, blocked); a note of ≤ 200 characters the reducer never reads
reviewerfw review --accept | --reject, refused if the reviewer owns or built the card
math-reviewerfw math:sign <decl>
any agentscreen, gate, run and device job requests; console-api runs the job and records the result

Coordination rules from the chat history

  • No recurring AI check prompts: console-api's watchers (device, stall, repeated notices) wake an agent only when something changes.
  • Workers send results to their consumer; the lead gets ≤ 300 characters and a file path.
  • Agents cannot write console state: a strict sandbox and deny rules guard the gitignored .fw-console/, and console-api is its only writer.
  • A wait of an hour or more ends the agent with a handoff note; a script spawns a fresh one.
  • After every compaction a hook re-injects the roster, names and the lead's address.
  • One plain command per Bash call; multi-step work is a committed pnpm fw command.
  • main moves only through the lead's fw land (ff-only); any other move shows up as a violation on the user's needs-you list.

Budget: looser, by the user's choice

Speed over token savings. No hard caps or stop rules: cost is reported daily against a forecast, with soft alerts for a milestone above 1.5× its forecast, a day above 2× the running average, or a cold-wake share above 10%. The one real stop is the provider's weekly usage limit, alerted at 60% and 80%.

Forecast ≈ $5,730 at list price, expected to run 20–40% higher with more Opus and concurrency; Lean-first adds about $700–1,100 of Lean work in place of $280 (both estimates).

reported per day: tokens by role · cache-read share · cold wakes · compactions · list-price $

A dependency graph, not a calendar

Roadmap

There are no dates. A workstream starts as soon as its inputs exist; independent ones run in parallel, each in its own worktree. Milestones M0–M6 are gates: conditions that must hold, not days. Time is measured, not planned: git history is the timeline, and the meter reports time and cost per gate.

WorkstreamBlocked byUnblocks
lean-core— (seeded from the sketches)fwcore serve with the console core, phone queue, ops, wire, Frames, Verdict; math-view lint → console-mvp, lean-m1+, store-and-run, M0
counts-chromiumthe local snapshotbyte-identical count vectors of the original, first V-a run → store-and-run, rule cards, M0
webkit-spike—Simulator counts per type on the original (time box 2 agent-days) → M1, rule cards, calibration
console-mvp landed 8bec088lean-core (a temporary TS reducer until then, checked by replay)step queue first; console-api as single writer; derived views; fw land → agent-ops, every device step
site-aot landed d380999—site scaffold, MUI theme, census route; SPK-r Chromium half passed → pilot parts
breakpoints landed a3e1e9cthe local snapshotthe inventory and the extracted breakpoints.json → lean-site
lean-sitebreakpoints (the extracted file as golden)the Lean breakpoint model; generates breakpoints.gen.json, media strings and the gate matrix → breakpoint lint and gate, pilot parts
agent-opsconsole-mvp (socket)sandbox block, hooks, role files, SPK-o/p/t → worktree agents commit; fw land the only way to main
store-and-runcounts-chromium, lean-corecount reduction and verdicts in fwcore; artifact store, fw run, harness-neutrality fixtures → M1

calibrationWebKit counts, K fixtures, the cloud-Mac spike, booked phone sessions (Q1)iPhone K1–K10, page factor, holdouts, validity table → M3

Gates: what must hold

GateReached when
M0 BootstrapTwo byte-identical Chromium count vectors for the original (or the failure recorded); fwcore serve behind console-api with the M0 Lean modules signed and every M0 mutant killed; the step queue live; the M0 spikes answered as decision records.
M1 Original measuredChromium count types deterministic; 0 sheet mutations on the original; WebKit's stable set covers fixtures K1–K9; per-zone baselines; SPK-r passed or a fallback chosen; v1 status replay and stall-alarm precision (≥ 90%) reported.
M2 Pilots faithful3 parts faithful, each through the breakpoint gate; breakpoints.json generated and its lint green; PL5 and N3 bands frozen from pilot data.
M3 CalibratedSimulator-to-phone count transfer and ranking checked on the phone; model status per output recorded; @layer mui kept or dropped from K10; first blind feel check scheduled.
M4 All parts promotedEvery part faithful or faithful-with-delta through the full breakpoint gate; Simulator check passed; per-module Lean evidence review.
M5 ExperimentsThe end-of-page behaviour decided first; the backlog run as flag arms, each known v1 outcome also a postdiction test; G1 reached; agreement measured on ≥ 10 changes.
M6 DistillWrite-up material complete; publishing is the user's call.
Review

Decisions

Everything the user decided on 2026-10-17 is applied in revision 5. One question is still open, to answer before the first phone session.

QuestionStatusAnswer
Q1 Phone sessionsopenWhich times of day, and how long a session? May the second iPhone stay a free-play device, kept out of measurement? Recommended: a few fixed windows a week; yes.
Q1 DevicesdecidediPhone 15 Pro Max on iOS 27.0.1 with Safari 27; Developer Mode allowed; no Android phone. The iOS 27.0 Simulator is installed to match; the Android emulator gives counts only.
Q2 Install LeandecidedYes. elan 4.2.4 from Homebrew's elan-init, Lean 4.35.0.
Q3 Repo visibilitydecidedPrivate. The no-copy rules still apply, so a later partial publication stays possible.
Q4 MUI scopedecidedMUI everywhere, with Emotion AOT on MUI 9.5; Base UI per part and Pigment on MUI 9.0.1 as fallbacks.
Q12 Lean scopedecidedLean-first, by milestone; mutants and a per-module demotion rule replace the M4 go/no-go.
Q16 BudgetdecidedLooser: speed first; costs reported with soft alerts, no hard stops.
Q22 SandboxdecidedYes, strict, for every agent; no unsandboxed retry.
Q23 Console locationdecidedInside the repo in the gitignored .fw-console/, written only by console-api. main stays a normal branch; a move outside fw land is flagged.
Q24 Lean firstdecidedEverything reproducible in the console, site, measurement and tooling is specified and proved in Lean before coding; Lean runs it, generates it, or provides golden vectors. fwcore is the console brain.
BreakpointsdecidedEvery breakpoint of the original, identically, for every part: generated list, lint, gate before promotion.
Console upkeepdecidedNobody writes status; every view is derived from the event log.
Reading proofsdecidedMath, not Lean: docstring math, a generated math view, a build gate, a math-reviewer role.
Lean packagingdecidedMathlib-free core; optional FwMath package for proofs that need Mathlib.
InstallsdecidedHomebrew whenever a formula or cask exists; otherwise ask the lead first.

Defaults Q25–Q30, used unless the user objects

DefaultWhat it means
Q25 Math viewA tab in console-web, also openable alone; math on every theorem and every definition the user reads.
Q26 Lease starvationNo renewing while someone waits, plus a cap on total hold time, with a bounded-wait theorem.
Q27 Aging stepA tighter bound than one level per 300 s: every job starts within 2 h of a booked window that fits it.
Q28 Math disagreementsA second independent reviewer decides first; the user sees only what stays unresolved.
Q29 Status questionsAnswered automatically from the board, with a "not answered" button that escalates to the lead.
Q30 Small defaultsNo auto-land for class W; no knowledge-base read receipts; an agent's ETA is shown but never scheduled on; the user picks among unbeaten best builds.
Earlier defaults the plan uses unless the user objects
  • Q5: look and work parity for experiment parts, look parity for the rest, every breakpoint for all parts; a time box per part.
  • Q6: the parity reference is snapshot b1789284481295-a455e793; v1's best build becomes the v1-best preset.
  • Q7: expect 5–10 phone sessions before the first licensed class; classes X and P always use the phone.
  • Q8: Chromium is a development aid with no fitted coefficients.
  • Q9: acceptance bands V-a to V-t; a licence is per change class.
  • Q10: no "less work" landing for style-affecting changes in WebKit until a test-runner element count exists; a 1-day spike on a cloud Mac before calibration.
  • Q11: optimized variants pass a compositor gate; 60 Hz is the canonical rate.
  • Q13: landing verdict 4 vs 4 runs, false-win rate at most 1/70 (to prove in M0, planned); 5 vs 5 (at most 1/252) or sequential when more than 3 comparisons.
  • Q14: question → build → screen → review → (device) → land, with classes W, SM, X, P.
  • Q15, Q19: raw traces and phone-screen recordings stay local.
  • Q17, Q18, Q20: one decision record on team operation after the M0 spikes; 1 h cache for short waits, handoff and exit for long ones; no recurring AI check prompts.
  • Q21: SPK-r decides; Base UI per part first, Pigment for the whole site only if AOT fails at the mechanism level.
